review_notes:
I read the whole file. I did not search the supplied roots, so this verdict rests on reading the file alone. The definitions are Point (an abbrev for ℕ ⊕ ℕ), leftTarget, rightTarget, family, rightTail, leftAnchors, rightAnchors and leftCore.

- Point, leftTarget, rightTarget and family are domain-specific constructions built from Sum.elim, Set.range and union. I found no Mathlib concept that they compete with.
- rightTail, leftAnchors and rightAnchors are already built on Mathlib's Finset.preimage. They are named wrappers that carry the injectivity proofs, so they are not competing versions.
- leftCore could be written as ⋂₀ {D | leftTarget i D ∈ active ..}, which is the set intersection already in Mathlib. That is only a restatement of a set-builder, and the named definition is used in later lemmas. I judged the consolidation case too weak to report.
- shift_infinite, right_part_infinite and right_target_left_finite are theorems that may overlap with existing lemmas. The rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication.
- The notions Generic.UUS, Valid, active and activeCore come from other files and are not defined here. I did not check them, so I make no claim about them.

Remaining uncertainty: I did not verify whether Mathlib has a competing notion for the anchored-family pattern itself. It looks specific to this development.
